description: We’re a team of 15-year-old students from Hyderabad, and this is our first time at NASA Space Apps. Between us we cover programming, design and data work, and most of it we’ve taught ourselves through side projects and trial and error. We split tasks based on what each of us is good at, pick up new tools quickly, and want to come out of the weekend with something that actually works.
summary:
This hyperlocalized map, made for a marswalk to Gediz Vallis, is a tool which helps an astronaut plan a surface excursion. They start above the Gediz Vallis range, on Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp), and end at the base of Gediz Vallis, where different layers of the mountain record the history of water on mars. The map includes route planning,  optical, topography, elevation bands, chemical analayze of nearby rocks, etc.. 
This helps astronauts avoid hazards, find optimal routes and navigate safely
details:
Our project takes data from satellites and previous rover exploration, processes and compiles it into one map. Our base interface is a panoramic view of mars seen from the inside of a helmet, with a mini map marking the current location on the top right. The default starting point is on Aeolis Mons and destination is the base of Gediz Vallis; both the start and end points can be moved around to simulate different situations. The colored topography of the rocks can toggled on & off by the menu on the right. Hovering over the map with your cursor gives Latitude, Longitude, and elevation(Coordinates and height).

Our project was made with the intent of creating clear hyperlocalized guides to areas with significance to the story of mars-past and future. You can see the route which previous rovers took while exploring areas close to yours with the data they found, which can leads to insights about chemical makeup of nearby rocks and soil.
